audit.description: Changed production code replaces the direct `requests` import in `coinbaseadvanced/client.py` with `import aiohttp`, and the added `_AiohttpRequestsAdapter._request` constructs `aiohttp.ClientTimeout`, opens `aiohttp.ClientSession`, and calls `session.request(...)`. The changed model files remove `requests` imports and use generic response helpers instead of `requests.Response` types. Static and dynamic evidence report no source imports from production repo code, target events from production `coinbaseadvanced/client.py`, and `aiohttp` resolving from site-packages with no local target provider.
evidence: diff coinbaseadvanced/client.py: `import requests` replaced by `import aiohttp`; `_request` uses `aiohttp.ClientTimeout`, `aiohttp.ClientSession`, and `session.request`.

diff coinbaseadvanced/client.py: request call sites changed from `requests.get/post/put/delete` to `_http_client.get/post/put/delete`; `requests = _http_client` is a local compatibility alias to the aiohttp-backed adapter, not an import of the source library.
diff model files: `import requests` removed from accounts.py, common.py, error.py, fees.py, orders.py, portfolios.py, and products.py; response annotations changed to `Any` and shared helpers.

dynamic evidence: first target import comes from production `coinbaseadvanced/client.py` line 15, with origin under site-packages `aiohttp/__init__.py`; `target_events_from_production_repo_count` is 15 and `target_local_spec_count` is 0.
static evidence: `coinbaseadvanced/client.py` has `imports_target: true`, `imports_source: false`, `fake_target_added_code: false`, and all checked production files passed.
reasons: Production code meaningfully uses real aiohttp APIs for HTTP requests.
Changed production files do not import or dynamically access requests.
No local aiohttp provider/shim is indicated; target origin is site-packages and target_local_spec_count is 0.

+            async with session.request(method, url, headers=headers, json=json_body) as response:
+                return _HttpResponse(response.status, await response.text())
